cards.explanation: The answer is today's date. God tells Ezekiel, “…write down today’s date…” Friends, I would have checked the calendar three times and still written it in pencil, just to be safe. God gives the reason right away: on this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem.

The answer is Jerusalem. God says that on this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to it. That's why the date matters, friends. Ezekiel is told to write it down so the day gets a place on the record.

The answer is True. God says, “Take the choicest of the flock and pile the fuel beneath it. Bring it to a boil and cook the bones in it.” The fuel goes under the pot first, and then comes the boil. Bakers, I've never been so glad my ovens come with a timer.

The answer is False. The king of Babylon appears earlier, laying siege to Jerusalem. In the woe, God says, “Woe to the city of bloodshed, to the pot now rusted, whose rust will not come off!” The pot is paired with the city, friends, not with the king.

The answer is on the bare rock. God says, “she poured it out on the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground to cover it with dust.” Bare rock has nothing to cover it. This is a heavy part, friends.

The answer is to stir up wrath and take vengeance. God's words are, “In order to stir up wrath and take vengeance, I have placed her blood on the bare rock, so that it would not be covered.” This is a heavy verse, friends.
The answer is burned. God says, “let the bones be burned.” Just before that, He says to pile on the logs and kindle the fire, friends.

The answer is that the heat will melt its impurity and burn off its rust. God says, “Then its impurity will melt within; its rust will be consumed.” The empty pot sits on the coals until it's hot and its copper glows. Bakers, I've scrubbed a baking sheet or two in my day, and I never once had this kind of heat to help.

The answer is False. God says the pot “…has frustrated every effort…” and that its thick rust “…has not been removed, even by the fire.” The rust is stuck on, friends. I've met a few stubborn stains in my time, but nothing like this.

The answer is cleanse. God says, “…I tried to cleanse you, but you would not be purified from your filthiness.” The pot talk has stopped, and now He's speaking straight to “you.” It's a heavy line, friends, and it's said plainly.

The answer is until His wrath has subsided. God says, “You will not be pure again until My wrath against you has subsided.” The verse gives that one condition, friends. This is a serious line, and it's good to let it be serious.
The answer is True. God says, “I will not refrain or show pity, nor will I relent.” It follows right after “the time is coming, and I will act.” This is a heavy line, friends.
The answer is your ways and deeds. God says, “I will judge you according to your ways and deeds…” That's how He closes the parable, friends. It's a heavy ending.
